+# Grafana HA with embedded NATS test setup

+A docker compose setup that runs three Grafana instances sharing one database, with embedded NATS turned on as described in [Set up NATS for high availability](../../../docs/sources/setup-grafana/set-up-nats-for-high-availability.md).
+Use it to try HA watches on the legacy SQL unified-storage backend by hand, the way a self-managed HA cluster runs them.
+Refer to the docs page for what each setting does, the port guidance and troubleshooting.
+- `db`: MySQL 8.4 (default) or Postgres 17, the shared Grafana database.
+- `grafana1`, `grafana2`, `grafana3`: Grafana with `[nats] enabled = true`, cluster TLS on the cluster port, and the same Secrets Manager `secret_key`.
+- `nginx-proxy`: round-robin reverse proxy in front of the three instances, the only port published on the host.
+- `smoke`: the smoke checks in `smoke/main.go`, built and started on demand, see [Smoke test](#smoke-test).
+Apart from cluster TLS and `advertise_address`, the instances use the `[nats]` defaults.
+They find each other through the shared database and bind the cluster port `6222` on all interfaces.
+Each instance advertises its hostname, `grafana1` to `grafana3`, and its certificate is issued for that name.

+Without `advertise_address`, an instance advertises the IP address of its network interface, so its certificate would need that IP as a SAN, and Docker assigns container IPs when the network is created and can change them on restart.
+The docs page recommends the same for any cluster whose instance IPs change.
+Port `6222` is only reachable on the compose network, and the client port `4222` stays closed.
+The instances start one after another, because concurrent first-start migrations race on the migration lock.
+Build an image from the branch you want to test:
+On Apple silicon, add `PLATFORM=linux/arm64` to avoid emulating amd64.
+To test a published build instead, set `GRAFANA_IMAGE`, for example `GRAFANA_IMAGE=grafana/grafana-dev:<tag>`.
+Run this and the following commands from this directory:
+This writes a CA, one certificate per instance with its hostname as the SAN, and a "rogue" certificate from a second CA into `certs/out` (gitignored).
+Each instance mounts its own directory at `/certs`.
+To test certificate rotation, regenerate the certificates while the stack runs: instances pick up changed files within about 15 seconds.
+Settings, all optional, read from the environment or a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yaml`:
+| `GRAFANA_IMAGE`              | `grafana/grafana-oss:dev` | Grafana image for all three instances                                                             |
+| `SECRETS_MANAGER_SECRET_KEY` | `ha-test-nats-secret-key` | `[secrets_manager.encryption.secret_key.v1] secret_key`, which encrypts the NATS route credential |
+This builds `smoke/main.go` into a small image and runs it on the compose network, so it reaches ports 3000, 6222 and 4222 of every instance without publishing them.
+It mounts the Docker socket to kill `grafana1`.
+- Notifier: every instance registers `grafana_storage_server_sql_watch_missing_events_total`, which the legacy SQL backend registers only with the NATS notifier.
+- Discovery: all three instances have a row in `nats_discovery_peers`.
+- Routes: `grafana_nats_embedded_server_routes` is 2, the number of instances minus one, on every instance.
+- Route credential: one row for it in `secret_encrypted_value`.
+- Watch fan-out: a playlist created on `grafana1` arrives as `ADDED` on watches opened on `grafana2` and `grafana3`.
+- No polling: right after the watch writes, `grafana_storage_server_poller_query_latency_seconds` has no samples on any instance.
+  A polling instance reads `resource_history` before it can deliver a write to its watch, so the check needs no idle window.
+- Mutual TLS on port 6222: a TLS connection with the CA and a node certificate gets the NATS route `INFO`; no client certificate, the rogue certificate and a plaintext connection get nothing.
+- Client port 4222 is closed on every instance.
+- Node loss: after a kill of `grafana1`, `grafana2` and `grafana3` drop to one route, and a surviving peer prunes the row of `grafana1`.

+  With the default discovery TTL (15s) and interval (5s), the prune takes at most 21s: the heartbeat is stored in whole seconds, so it goes stale up to TTL plus 1s after the kill, and the next tick of a peer prunes it within one interval.
+  The check waits for both conditions for up to 26s, one more interval of margin for a slow or failed prune tick.
+It prints `PASS` or `FAIL` per check and exits with the number of failures.
+`SKIP_KILL=1` skips the last check, for example `docker compose run --rm -e SKIP_KILL=1 smoke`.
+After the kill check, bring the instance back with `docker compose up -d --wait grafana1`.
+Use the same `GRAFANA_DB` for the smoke test as for `docker compose up`.
+The database runs on tmpfs, so `down` discards all data.
+# Generates the certificates for the ha-test-nats setup into certs/out:
+#   out/ca.crt                          CA that signs every node certificate
+#   out/grafanaN/{node.crt,node.key,ca.crt}  one directory per Grafana node, mounted at /certs
+#   out/rogue/{node.crt,node.key}       a certificate for grafana1 signed by a second, untrusted CA
+# Node certificates carry both serverAuth and clientAuth because every instance
+# accepts and dials cluster routes. Their only SAN is the node hostname, which is
+# what each instance advertises to its peers.
+# Keep the directories: running containers bind-mount out/grafanaN and would not see recreated ones.
+	# Grafana runs as uid 472 in the container and must read the bind-mounted key.
+    # Query over TCP: the init server the entrypoint runs first only listens on the socket,
+    # so a socket ping reports healthy before the real server accepts Grafana's connections.
+    # Check over TCP: the init server the entrypoint runs first only listens on the socket.
+# The smoke checks find the containers by name, so the project name is fixed.
+  # Instances start one after another: concurrent first-start migrations race on the migration lock.
+  # Each one advertises its hostname: container IPs change on restart, and the certificates carry DNS names only.
+  # Runs the smoke checks from inside the compose network, so ports 6222 and 4222 are never published.
+  # Start it with `docker compose run --rm --build smoke`.
+      # The node loss check kills grafana1.
+    # Self-heals a transient startup failure, such as the database not accepting connections yet.
+      # The background plugin installer blocks shutdown while grafana.com is slow or unreachable.
+      # Secrets Manager encrypts the NATS route credential under this key, so every instance needs the same one.
+# Re-resolve the instances through Docker's DNS: a recreated container can get a new IP.
+// Command smoke checks the ha-test-nats setup. It runs in the smoke service on the
+// compose network, so it reaches every instance's ports 3000, 6222 and 4222 without
+// publishing them, and it kills grafana1 through the mounted Docker socket.
+	if s.db, err = openDB(s.dbType); err != nil {
+	s.section("Waiting for all Grafana instances (up to 120s)")
+	if err := s.waitHealthy(120 * time.Second); err != nil {
+		fmt.Printf("FAIL: %v; start the stack with 'docker compose up -d --wait' first\n", err)
+				return fmt.Errorf("grafana%d is not healthy", n)
+// checkNotifier relies on the legacy SQL backend registering this counter only when it
+// builds its NATS notifier, which replaces the polling one.
+	s.section("Notifier: every instance serves watches from NATS")
+	s.section("Discovery: every instance registers a route in nats_discovery_peers")
+		if peers, err = s.peers(); err == nil && len(peers) >= 3 {
+	s.section("Routes: grafana_nats_embedded_server_routes is 2 on every instance")
+		for deadline := time.Now().Add(2 * discoveryInterval); time.Now().Before(deadline); time.Sleep(time.Second) {
+	s.section("Route credential: stored as a Secrets Manager encrypted value")
+	err := s.db.QueryRow("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM secret_encrypted_value WHERE namespace = 'default' AND name = 'nats:grafana.route-credential'").Scan(&count)
+	s.check(count == 1, "route credential: %d row in secret_encrypted_value (expected 1)", count)
+	s.section("Watch fan-out: create a playlist on grafana1, watch it on grafana2 and grafana3")
+	code, err := s.do(ctx, http.MethodPost, "http://grafana1:3000"+api, playlist, nil)
+	fmt.Printf("  create on grafana1: HTTP %d %v\n", code, errOrEmpty(err))
+			s.pass("watch: grafana%d saw ADDED (%dms)", n, at.Sub(created).Milliseconds())
+			s.fail("watch: grafana%d did not see ADDED within 15s", n)
+// openWatch starts a watch on instance n from its current list resource version, so only
+// the new write can match, not the initial state.
+	if _, err := s.do(ctx, http.MethodGet, base, "", &list); err != nil {
+	// The shared client's timeout would end the watch early; ctx bounds it instead.
+func waitForAdded(body io.ReadCloser, name string, seen chan<- time.Time) {
+	// GetClientCertificate presents the certificate even when the server's acceptable CAs
+	// don't include its issuer; with Certificates, Go would send no certificate for the rogue one.
+			c.GetClientCertificate = func(*tls.CertificateRequestInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error) { return cert, nil }
+		s.pass("tls: CA + node cert completes the handshake and gets the route INFO")
+		s.fail("tls: CA + node cert: %q %v", line, err)
+	s.check(!strings.HasPrefix(line, "INFO"), "tls: no client cert is rejected (%v)", err)
+	s.check(!strings.HasPrefix(line, "INFO"), "tls: rogue CA cert is rejected (%v)", err)
+	s.check(!strings.Contains(line, "INFO"), "tls: plaintext connection gets no route INFO")
+// routeGreeting connects to grafana2's cluster port, over TLS unless config is nil, and
+// returns the first line the server sends.
+		s.check(err != nil, "client port: grafana%d:4222 closed", n)
+// checkNoPolling runs right after the watch writes instead of over an idle window: a
+// polling notifier reads resource_history only once the latest resource versions change,
+// and a polling instance can only have delivered those writes to its watch after such a
+// read, so a zero count involves no timing.
+			s.fail("no polling: grafana%d metrics: %v", n, err)
+			s.fail("no polling: grafana%d exposes no grafana_storage_server_poller_query_latency_seconds", n)
+		s.check(polls == 0, "no polling: grafana%d made %v resource_history polls", n, polls)
+// checkKill kills grafana1 and waits until a surviving peer prunes its row and both peers
+// The deadline follows pkg/infra/nats/discovery.go: a heartbeat stores updatedAt in whole
+// seconds, and the row is stale once updatedAt < now - ttl, so a heartbeat just before the
+// kill goes stale ttl + 1s later. Only a surviving peer's tick prunes it, and ticks run every
+// interval with no jitter, so the worst case is ttl + 1s + interval. One more interval of
+// margin covers a slow or failed prune tick, which is retried on the next one.
+	s.section(fmt.Sprintf("Kill grafana1: its peer row is pruned and peers drop its route (worst case %s, deadline %s)", worst, deadline))
+			fmt.Printf("  last grafana1 heartbeat (updatedAt, whole seconds) %ds before the kill\n", time.Now().Unix()-p.UpdatedAt)
+			if peers, err := s.peers(); err == nil && !containsGrafana1(peers) {
+	s.check(rowGone > 0, "kill: grafana1 peer row gone %s", after(rowGone, deadline))
+	s.check(routes2 > 0, "kill: grafana2 has 1 route %s", after(routes2, deadline))
+	s.check(routes3 > 0, "kill: grafana3 has 1 route %s", after(routes3, deadline))
